pit_profile.why: FY19 10-K: 'We are an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the acquisition, development, exploration and exploitation of unconventional, onshore oil and natural gas reserves in the Permian Basin in West Texas.' Risk factors: 'The oil and natural gas industry is cyclical, which can result in shortages of drilling rigs, equipment, raw materials (particularly sand and other proppants), supplies and personnel.' and 'Our revenues, operating results, profitability, future rate of growth and the carrying value of our oil and natural gas properties depend significantly upon the prevailing prices for oil and natural gas.' The kind is CYCLICAL on the 10-K's own word for its industry (the CB and LYB rule): the earnings are the oil price; of the live disruption themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution', STREAMING to 'cord-cutting / streaming displaces linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles', EV to 'battery-electric vehicles displace ICE powertrains, auto parts suppliers and fuel retail', CRYPTO to 'crypto / DeFi disintermediates payments networks, banks, exchanges, remittance': none names an oil and gas producer; EV's 'fuel retail' names no Diamondback business (it produces and sells crude oil, natural gas and NGLs, and has no retail outlets), and the FY19 10-K's 'Conservation measures and technological advances could reduce demand for oil and natural gas.' is the demand risk ENERGY_TRANSITION already carries on the watch list; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12, scoped to 'decarbonisation strands oil, gas and coal reserves and refining'): Diamondback's reserves are oil and gas and its climate legislation risk factor puts the theme on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Diamondback

theme_watch.reason: Live: Diamondback's own FY19 10-K says 'Regulation of greenhouse gas emissions could result in increased operating costs and reduced demand for the oil and natural gas we produce.' The stock trades at 7.9x FY20E — a discount to its own history. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ENERGY_TRANSITION) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing decarbonisation of Diamondback's oil and gas reserves specifically.

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY13-FY18 ex-FY15 ex-FY16, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -46.3%/yr (Q3 revenues + margin + buyback); P/E at its 8.1-yr ex-FY12 ex-FY15 ex-FY16 ex-FY19 median

BULL.desc: EPS +44.3%/yr (FY13-FY18 ex-FY15 ex-FY16 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +44.3%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY13-FY18 ex-FY15 ex-FY16: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: FANG (retrospective, 2021-01-22) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.08x (35.7% downside to Bear $41 / +452.2% upside to Bull $352) | Adj composite 1.95 vs market 1.56: gap +0.39 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | -28% above the EPP floor $89 (11x FY20E $8.06) | Conservative 2-yr case: +119.8% total (+59.9%/yr) | At 7.9x FY20E the 15% hurdle price $84 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; oil-equivalent production +0.1% and oil production -8.3% in Q3 2020, forward revenues -26.1% (no FY20 revenue guide in numbers, Q3 2020 revenues as reported); the energy transition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
